evidence.supports: Official county public notice of the proposed ordinance's text (one-year moratorium on data centers in unincorporated areas), the August 11, 2026 public hearing date, and that adoption could be considered at the August 25, 2026 commission meeting.
evidence.quote: An Ordinance for a Data Center Moratorium. ... This ordinance prohibits the establishment or expansion of any data center in unincorporated areas of the County. ... This ordinance will be in effect for one year. ... The Colfax County Commissioners may consider adoption of the ordinance on Tuesday, August 25, 2026.

evidence.supports: Confirms the ordinance passed unanimously ('late last month,' i.e. late August 2026), its one-year term, its scope (unincorporated areas only, not municipalities like Raton), and commissioners' stated water/drought and noise rationale.
evidence.quote: Colfax County, N.M., commissioners voted to put a stop to building data centers in the unincorporated parts of the county for one year. The ordinance passed unanimously late last month.

evidence.supports: Corroborates that the August 11, 2026 commission meeting moved the proposed one-year moratorium forward toward adoption.
evidence.quote: Concerns about water use and the potential effects of large-scale data centers dominated the Aug. 11 meeting of the Colfax County Board of Commissioners, where commissioners moved forward with a proposed one-year moratorium on new data center development in unincorporated areas of the county.

decisions.notes: Verified against the county's own public notice (Ordinance No. 2026-02 text, one-year term, Aug. 25, 2026 consideration date) and CPR.org's confirmation the ordinance 'passed unanimously late last month.' Scope correctly limited to unincorporated areas (Raton and other municipalities not bound). No duplicate.
